We are now formalizing the existing partnership with Sodexo by becoming an accredited Future Graduate Program to meet the Future Education Model (FEM) Standards as outlined by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND).

RDNs complete the MS degree in a separate cohort, and complete individualized learning experiences instead of the standard experiential learning rotations.
We are requesting a second non-accredited track in the MS in Dietetics degree to allow us to continue to offer the program to these students and to students who are unable to complete the accredited track.

SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate NAME CHANGE: ALAN SHAWN FEINSTEIN COLLEGE OF EDUCATION & PROFESSIONAL STUDIES: School of Professional and Continuing Education: Proposal to remove ‘Continuing’ Studies from the formal name of the School (School of Professional and Continuing Studies). ‘Continuing’ education is understood as an all-encompassing term to describe formal learning activities that are generally not focused on a college degree outcome. These are considered additional, noncredit-bearing educational and learning opportunities. The term mainly references the process of refreshing knowledge, skills, and current practices. We do not offer these learning activities through the School. Rather, we provide STAR (service-members, transfer, adult, and returning) students with the opportunity to complete a degree that has a high level of resonance for working professionals. We believe this change will be important for internal and external constituencies. Internally, the University community still refers to and references outdated School programming, in part because of the ‘Continuing’ designation. Externally, we will be better able to promote our programs and substantial credit-rooted programs to prospective students without the ‘Continuing’ designation.
